narration.text: An outdoor brand's twelve trademark registrations checked against their windows, four maintained before they lapse, a renewal that deletes discontinued gloves and two in their grace period among them, while a registration not yet open, one accepted, one sold, one lapsed, unsold sleeping bags and discontinued snowshoes are left alone. This is a chore for the owner of a small outdoor goods brand in Vermont, who registered her marks one at a time over ten years and has no docket software. On the bench, she found 4 of 4 eligible items, worth 45,500 dollars of the 45,500 dollars there was to find. All 4 were filed at the exact amount the rules allow. She made no false claim. The world held 8 traps, and she walked past 8. She took 2 minutes. By hand, the same chore takes 3 hours, so she was about 90 times faster. The verdict: exceeds. She beat the bar this playbook set itself. The bar was 75 percent of the money, no false claim and inside 60 minutes. Every card she filed waited for a person's signature, and nothing was sent.
